claim: Neural responses within the sensory cortices are inherently transient.
source: Neural responses within the sensory cortices are inherently transient.
evidence: This is a general statement about sensory cortices supported by established scientific knowledge.

claim: In the auditory cortex, even the simplest stimulus, for instance a pure tone, evokes neural responses that strongly vary in time following the onset and offset of the stimulus.
source: In the auditory cortex (AC) even the simplest stimulus, for instance a pure tone, evokes neural responses that strongly vary in time following the onset and offset of the stimulus.
evidence: This is a general observation about auditory cortex responses supported by established knowledge.

claim: A number of past studies have reported a prevalence of ON- compared to OFF-responsive neurons in different auditory areas.
source: A number of past studies have reported a prevalence of ON- compared to OFF-responsive neurons in different auditory areas (Phillips et al., 2002; Luo et al., 2008; Fu et al., 2010; Pollak and Bodenhamer, 1981).
evidence: This claim is supported by citations to previous studies.

claim: The transient onset component has been long considered the dominant feature of auditory responses and has been extensively studied across the auditory pathway.
source: As a result, the transient onset component has been long considered the dominant feature of auditory responses and has been extensively studied across the auditory pathway (Liu et al., 2019b; Kuwada and Batra, 1999; Grothe et al., 1992; Guo and Burkard, 2002; Yu et al., 2004; Heil, 1997a; Heil, 1997b), with respect to its neurophysiological basis and perceptual meaning (Phillips et al., 2002).
evidence: This claim is supported by multiple citations to previous studies.

claim: OFF responses have been observed in awake animals throughout the auditory pathway.
source: Yet, OFF responses have been observed in awake animals throughout the auditory pathway, and in the mouse AC they arise in 30–70% of the responsive neurons (Scholl et al., 2010; Keller et al., 2018; Joachimsthaler et al., 2014; Liu et al., 2019a; Sollini et al., 2018).
evidence: This claim is supported by citations to previous studies.

claim: In the mouse AC, OFF responses arise in 30–70% of the responsive neurons.
source: Yet, OFF responses have been observed in awake animals throughout the auditory pathway, and in the mouse AC they arise in 30–70% of the responsive neurons (Scholl et al., 2010; Keller et al., 2018; Joachimsthaler et al., 2014; Liu et al., 2019a; Sollini et al., 2018).
evidence: This claim is supported by citations to previous studies.

claim: The generation of ON responses has been attributed to neural mechanisms based on short-term adaptation, most likely inherited from the auditory nerve fibers.
source: While the generation of ON responses has been attributed to neural mechanisms based on short-term adaptation, most likely inherited from the auditory nerve fibers (Phillips et al., 2002; Smith and Brachman, 1980; Smith and Brachman, 1982), the mechanisms that generate OFF responses are more diverse and seem to be area-specific (Xu et al., 2014; Kopp-Scheinpflug et al., 2018).
evidence: This claim is supported by citations to previous studies.

claim: The mechanisms that generate OFF responses are more diverse and seem to be area-specific.
source: While the generation of ON responses has been attributed to neural mechanisms based on short-term adaptation, most likely inherited from the auditory nerve fibers (Phillips et al., 2002; Smith and Brachman, 1980; Smith and Brachman, 1982), the mechanisms that generate OFF responses are more diverse and seem to be area-specific (Xu et al., 2014; Kopp-Scheinpflug et al., 2018).
evidence: This claim is supported by citations to previous studies.

claim: In subcortical regions, neurons in the dorsal cochlear nucleus and in the superior paraolivary nucleus of the brainstem nuclei may generate OFF responses by post-inhibitory rebound.
source: In subcortical regions, neurons in the dorsal cochlear nucleus and in the superior paraolivary nucleus of the brainstem nuclei may generate OFF responses by post-inhibitory rebound, a synaptic mechanism in which a neuron emits one or more spikes following the cessation of a prolonged hyperpolarizing current (Suga, 1964; Hancock and Voigt, 1999; Kopp-Scheinpflug et al., 2011).
evidence: This claim is supported by citations to previous studies.

claim: In the midbrain inferior colliculus and in the medial geniculate body of the thalamus, OFF responses appear to be mediated by excitatory inputs from upstream areas and potentially boosted by a post-inhibitory facilitation mechanism.
source: In the midbrain inferior colliculus and in the medial geniculate body of the thalamus, OFF responses appear to be mediated by excitatory inputs from upstream areas and potentially boosted by a post-inhibitory facilitation mechanism (Kasai et al., 2012; Vater et al., 1992; Yu et al., 2004; He, 2003).
evidence: This claim is supported by citations to previous studies.

claim: OFF responses in AC do not appear to be driven by hyperpolarizing inputs during the presentation of the stimulus, since synaptic inhibition has been found to be only transient with respect to the stimulus duration.
source: Unlike in subcortical areas, OFF responses in AC do not appear to be driven by hyperpolarizing inputs during the presentation of the stimulus, since synaptic inhibition has been found to be only transient with respect to the stimulus duration (Qin et al., 2007; Scholl et al., 2010).
evidence: This claim is supported by citations to previous studies.

claim: The precise cellular or network mechanisms underlying transient OFF responses in cortical areas remain to be fully elucidated.
source: The precise cellular or network mechanisms underlying transient OFF responses in cortical areas therefore remain to be fully elucidated.
evidence: This is a statement about the current state of knowledge in the field.

claim: Previous studies investigating the transient responses in the auditory system mostly adopted a single-neuron perspective.
source: Previous studies investigating the transient responses in the auditory system mostly adopted a single-neuron perspective (Henry, 1985; Scholl et al., 2010; Qin et al., 2007; He, 2002; Wang et al., 2005; Wang, 2007).
evidence: This claim is supported by citations to previous studies.

claim: In recent years, population approaches to neural data have proven valuable for understanding the role of transients dynamics in various cortical areas.
source: However, in recent years, population approaches to neural data have proven valuable for understanding the role of transients dynamics in various cortical areas (Buonomano and Maass, 2009; Remington et al., 2018; Saxena and Cunningham, 2019).
evidence: This claim is supported by citations to previous studies.

claim: Work in the olfactory system has shown that ON and OFF responses encode the stimulus identity in the dynamical patterns of activity across the neural population.
source: Work in the olfactory system has shown that ON and OFF responses encode the stimulus identity in the dynamical patterns of activity across the neural population (Mazor and Laurent, 2005; Stopfer et al., 2003; Broome et al., 2006; Friedrich and Laurent, 2001; Saha et al., 2017).
evidence: This claim is supported by citations to previous studies.

claim: In motor and premotor cortex, transient responses during movement execution form complex population trajectories.
source: In motor and premotor cortex, transient responses during movement execution form complex population trajectories (Churchland and Shenoy, 2007; Churchland et al., 2010) that have been hypothesized to be generated by a mechanism based on recurrent network dynamics (Shenoy et al., 2011; Hennequin et al., 2014; Sussillo et al., 2015; Stroud et al., 2018).
evidence: This claim is supported by citations to previous studies.

claim: Complex population trajectories in motor and premotor cortex have been hypothesized to be generated by a mechanism based on recurrent network dynamics.
source: In motor and premotor cortex, transient responses during movement execution form complex population trajectories (Churchland and Shenoy, 2007; Churchland et al., 2010) that have been hypothesized to be generated by a mechanism based on recurrent network dynamics (Shenoy et al., 2011; Hennequin et al., 2014; Sussillo et al., 2015; Stroud et al., 2018).
evidence: This claim is supported by citations to previous studies.

claim: Previous works have suggested a central role of the neural dynamics across large populations for the coding of different auditory features in the AC.
source: In the AC, previous works have suggested a central role of the neural dynamics across large populations for the coding of different auditory features (Deneux et al., 2016; Saha et al., 2017; Lim et al., 2016), yet how these dynamics are generated remains an open question.
evidence: This claim is supported by citations to previous studies.

claim: How neural dynamics in the AC are generated remains an open question.
source: In the AC, previous works have suggested a central role of the neural dynamics across large populations for the coding of different auditory features (Deneux et al., 2016; Saha et al., 2017; Lim et al., 2016), yet how these dynamics are generated remains an open question.
evidence: This is a statement about the current state of knowledge in the field.

claim: The AC constitutes a network of neurons connected in a recurrent fashion.
source: Leveraging the observation that the AC constitutes a network of neurons connected in a recurrent fashion (Linden and Schreiner, 2003; Oswald and Reyes, 2008; Oswald et al., 2009; Barbour and Callaway, 2008; Bizley et al., 2015), in this study we test the hypothesis that transient OFF responses are generated by a recurrent network mechanism broadly analogous to the motor cortex (Churchland et al., 2006; Hennequin et al., 2014).
evidence: This claim is supported by citations to previous studies.

claim: This study tests the hypothesis that transient OFF responses are generated by a recurrent network mechanism broadly analogous to the motor cortex.
source: Leveraging the observation that the AC constitutes a network of neurons connected in a recurrent fashion (Linden and Schreiner, 2003; Oswald and Reyes, 2008; Oswald et al., 2009; Barbour and Callaway, 2008; Bizley et al., 2015), in this study we test the hypothesis that transient OFF responses are generated by a recurrent network mechanism broadly analogous to the motor cortex (Churchland et al., 2006; Hennequin et al., 2014).
evidence: This is a statement of the study's hypothesis.

claim: OFF responses correspond to transiently amplified trajectories of population activity.
source: These analyses identified three prominent features of the auditory cortical data: (i) OFF responses correspond to transiently amplified trajectories of population activity; (ii) for each stimulus, the corresponding trajectory explores a low-dimensional subspace; and (iii) responses to different stimuli lie mostly in orthogonal subspaces.
evidence: This claim is based on analyses of auditory cortical data presented in the study.

claim: For each stimulus, the corresponding trajectory explores a low-dimensional subspace.
source: These analyses identified three prominent features of the auditory cortical data: (i) OFF responses correspond to transiently amplified trajectories of population activity; (ii) for each stimulus, the corresponding trajectory explores a low-dimensional subspace; and (iii) responses to different stimuli lie mostly in orthogonal subspaces.
evidence: This claim is based on analyses of auditory cortical data presented in the study.

claim: Responses to different stimuli lie mostly in orthogonal subspaces.
source: These analyses identified three prominent features of the auditory cortical data: (i) OFF responses correspond to transiently amplified trajectories of population activity; (ii) for each stimulus, the corresponding trajectory explores a low-dimensional subspace; and (iii) responses to different stimuli lie mostly in orthogonal subspaces.
evidence: This claim is based on analyses of auditory cortical data presented in the study.

claim: The single-cell model can reproduce the first two features of population dynamics in response to individual stimuli, but cannot capture the structure across stimuli and single trials.
source: We show that the single-cell model can reproduce the first two features of population dynamics in response to individual stimuli, but cannot capture the structure across stimuli and single trials.
evidence: This claim is based on model fitting and comparison presented in the study.

claim: The network model accounts for all three features of auditory cortical OFF responses.
source: In contrast, the network model accounted for the low-dimensional organization of population responses and their global structure across stimuli, where distinct stimuli activated mostly orthogonal dimensions in the neural state-space.
evidence: This claim is based on model fitting and comparison presented in the study.

claim: The network model accounts for the low-dimensional organization of population responses.
source: In contrast, the network model accounted for the low-dimensional organization of population responses and their global structure across stimuli, where distinct stimuli activated mostly orthogonal dimensions in the neural state-space.
evidence: This claim is based on model fitting and comparison presented in the study.

claim: Distinct stimuli activated mostly orthogonal dimensions in the neural state-space.
source: In contrast, the network model accounted for the low-dimensional organization of population responses and their global structure across stimuli, where distinct stimuli activated mostly orthogonal dimensions in the neural state-space.
evidence: This claim is based on analyses of auditory cortical data presented in the study.

claim: The neurons were recorded while the mice passively listened to auditory stimuli.
source: The neurons were recorded while the mice passively listened to randomized presentations of different auditory stimuli.
evidence: This is a description of the experimental setup.

claim: A total of 16 stimuli were considered, consisting of two groups of intensity modulated UP- or DOWN-ramping sounds.
source: In this study we consider a total of 16 stimuli, consisting of two groups of intensity modulated UP- or DOWN-ramping sounds.
evidence: This is a description of the stimuli used in the study.

claim: The activity of individual neurons to different stimuli was highly heterogeneous.
source: The activity of individual neurons to different stimuli was highly heterogeneous.
evidence: This claim is based on observations of neural activity data presented in the study.

claim: Individual neurons were found that were strongly active only during the onset of the stimulus (ON responses), or only during the offset (OFF responses), while other neurons in the population responded to both stimulus onset and offset.
source: In response to a single stimulus, we found individual neurons that were strongly active only during the onset of the stimulus (ON responses), or only during the offset (OFF responses), while other neurons in the population responded to both stimulus onset and offset, consistent with previous analyses (Deneux et al., 2016).
evidence: This claim is based on observations of neural activity data presented in the study and is consistent with previous analyses.

claim: Some neurons in the population exhibited ON and/or OFF responses only when specific stimuli were presented, showing stimulus-selectivity of transient responses.
source: Importantly, across stimuli some neurons in the population exhibited ON and/or OFF responses only when specific stimuli were presented, showing stimulus-selectivity of transient responses, while others strongly responded at the onset and/or at the offset of multiple stimuli (Figure 1A).
evidence: This claim is based on observations of neural activity data presented in the study and illustrated in Figure 1A.

claim: The distance from baseline computed during ON and OFF responses was larger than the distance computed for the state at the end of stimulus presentation.
source: This revealed that the distance from baseline computed during ON and OFF responses was larger than the distance computed for the state at the end of stimulus presentation (Figure 1B right panel).
evidence: This claim is based on analysis of population activity data presented in the study and illustrated in Figure 1B.

claim: The classification accuracy was highest during the transient phases corresponding to ON and OFF responses, while it decreased at the end of stimulus presentation.
source: We found that the classification accuracy was highest during the transient phases corresponding to ON and OFF responses, while it decreased at the end of stimulus presentation (Figure 1C).
evidence: This claim is based on decoding analysis of neural activity data presented in the study and illustrated in Figure 1C.

claim: The classification accuracy result revealed a robust encoding of the stimulus features during ON and OFF responses.
source: This result revealed a robust encoding of the stimulus features during ON and OFF responses, as previously found in the locust olfactory system (Mazor and Laurent, 2005; Saha et al., 2017).
evidence: This claim is based on decoding analysis of neural activity data presented in the study and is consistent with previous findings in the olfactory system.

claim: The dynamics during the transient OFF responses to individual stimuli explored only about five dimensions.
source: By performing principal component analysis (PCA) independently for the responses to individual stimuli, we found that the dynamics during the transient OFF responses to individual stimuli explored only about five dimensions, as 80% of the variance of the OFF responses to individual stimuli was explained on average by the first five principal components (Figure 2A; see Figure 2—figure supplement 1 for cross-validated controls; note that, given the temporal resolution, the maximal dimensionality explaining 80% of the variance of the responses to individual stimuli was 9).
evidence: This claim is based on PCA analysis of neural activity data presented in the study and illustrated in Figure 2A.

claim: 80% of the variance of the OFF responses to individual stimuli was explained on average by the first five principal components.
source: By performing principal component analysis (PCA) independently for the responses to individual stimuli, we found that the dynamics during the transient OFF responses to individual stimuli explored only about five dimensions, as 80% of the variance of the OFF responses to individual stimuli was explained on average by the first five principal components (Figure 2A; see Figure 2—figure supplement 1 for cross-validated controls; note that, given the temporal resolution, the maximal dimensionality explaining 80% of the variance of the responses to individual stimuli was 9).
evidence: This claim is based on PCA analysis of neural activity data presented in the study and illustrated in Figure 2A.

claim: The projection of the low-dimensional OFF responses to each stimulus onto the first two principal components revealed circular activity patterns, where the population vector smoothly rotated between the two dominant dimensions.
source: The projection of the low-dimensional OFF responses to each stimulus onto the first two principal components revealed circular activity patterns, where the population vector smoothly rotated between the two dominant dimensions (Figure 2B).
evidence: This claim is based on PCA analysis of neural activity data presented in the study and illustrated in Figure 2B.

claim: Stimuli with different frequency content evoked in general non-overlapping OFF responses reflected in low values of the subspace overlap.
source: This approach revealed an interesting structure between the OFF response subspaces for different stimuli (Figure 2D and Figure 2—figure supplement 2). Stimuli with different frequency content evoked in general non-overlapping OFF responses reflected in low values of the subspace overlap.
evidence: This claim is based on analysis of subspace overlaps of neural activity data presented in the study and illustrated in Figure 2D.

claim: Two clusters of correlated OFF responses emerged, corresponding to the 8 kHz UP-ramps and WN UP-ramps of different durations and intensity.
source: Two clusters of correlated OFF responses emerged, corresponding to the 8 kHz UP-ramps and WN UP-ramps of different durations and intensity.
evidence: This claim is based on analysis of subspace overlaps of neural activity data presented in the study.

claim: DOWN-ramps evoked OFF responses that were less correlated than UP-ramps, even for sounds with the same frequency content.
source: Surprisingly, DOWN-ramps evoked OFF responses that were less correlated than UP-ramps, even for sounds with the same frequency content.
evidence: This claim is based on analysis of subspace overlaps of neural activity data presented in the study.

claim: The number of principal components that explain 80% of the variance for all OFF responses considered together is around 60.
source: The fact that most of the stimuli evoked non-overlapping OFF responses is reflected in the number of principal components that explain 80% of the variance for all OFF responses considered together, which is around 60 (Figure 2C and Figure 2—figure supplement 1).
evidence: This claim is based on PCA analysis of neural activity data presented in the study and illustrated in Figure 2C.

claim: While the OFF responses to individual stimuli span low-dimensional subspaces, the joint response across stimuli shows high-dimensional structure.
source: Notably this implies that while the OFF responses to individual stimuli span low-dimensional subspaces, the joint response across stimuli shows high-dimensional structure.
evidence: This claim is based on inference from PCA analysis of neural activity data presented in the study.

claim: The initial states exhibited structure across stimuli that matched well the structure of OFF response dynamics.
source: Remarkably, we found that the initial states exhibited structure across stimuli that matched well the structure of OFF response dynamics (Figure 2E left panel and Figure 2—figure supplement 4), even though the component along the initial states was substracted from the corresponding OFF response trajectories (Figure 2E right panel and Figure 2—figure supplement 4).
evidence: This claim is based on analysis of initial states and OFF response dynamics presented in the study and illustrated in Figure 2E.

claim: Initial states contribute to determining the subsequent dynamics of the OFF responses.
source: This suggests that initial states contribute to determining the subsequent dynamics of the OFF responses.
evidence: This claim is based on inference from analysis of initial states and OFF response dynamics presented in the study.

claim: The single-cell model could not account for the structure of responses across multiple stimuli.
source: However, we found that the single-cell model could not account for the structure of responses across multiple stimuli.
evidence: This claim is based on model fitting and comparison presented in the study.

claim: In the single-cell model the temporal shape of the response of each neuron is the same across all stimuli, while this was not the case in the data.
source: A simple explanation for this inability to capture structure across stimuli is that in the single-cell model the temporal shape of the response of each neuron is the same across all stimuli, while this was not the case in the data (Figure 3E).
evidence: This claim is based on comparison of model predictions and data presented in the study and illustrated in Figure 3E.

claim: The fitted network model reproduced well the first two features of the data, transient amplification and low-dimensional population trajectories.
source: Qualitatively, we found that the fitted network model reproduced well the first two features of the data, transient amplification and low-dimensional population trajectories (Figure 3G,H).
evidence: This claim is based on model fitting and comparison presented in the study and illustrated in Figure 3G and 3H.

claim: When fitted to all stimuli at once, the fitted network model captured the structure of the subspace overlaps.
source: When fitted to all stimuli at once, the fitted network model captured the structure of the subspace overlaps (Figure 3I left panel) and its correlation with the structure of initial conditions (Figure 3I right panel).
evidence: This claim is based on model fitting and comparison presented in the study and illustrated in Figure 3I.

claim: The network model accounted well for the third feature of the data, the structure of responses across stimuli.
source: In contrast to the single-cell model, the network model therefore accounted well for the third feature of the data, the structure of responses across stimuli.
evidence: This claim is based on model fitting and comparison presented in the study.

claim: In the network model, the temporal OFF-responses of single cells can in general differ across stimuli.
source: This can be explained by the fact that, in the network model, the temporal OFF-responses of single cells can in general differ across stimuli (see Figure 6A,D), similar to the activity in the AC (Figure 3E).
evidence: This claim is based on model properties and comparison with data presented in the study and illustrated in Figure 6A, 6D, and 3E.

claim: The eigenvalues of the fitted connectivity matrix had real parts smaller than one, indicating stable dynamics, and large imaginary parts.
source: The eigenvalues of the fitted connectivity matrix had real parts smaller than one, indicating stable dynamics, and large imaginary parts (Figure 4A).
evidence: This claim is based on analysis of the fitted connectivity matrix presented in the study and illustrated in Figure 4A.

claim: The symmetric part of the connectivity had a large number of eigenvalues larger than one.
source: Consistent with this predictions, we found that the symmetric part of the connectivity had indeed a large number of eigenvalues larger than one (Figure 4B) and could therefore produce amplified responses (Figure 3G).
evidence: This claim is based on analysis of the fitted connectivity matrix presented in the study and illustrated in Figure 4B.

claim: The correlation between the peak state and the initial state at the end of stimulus presentation took values lower than values predicted by chance for almost all stimuli.
source: Finally, computing the correlation between the peak state and the initial state at the end of stimulus presentation, we found that this correlation took values lower than values predicted by chance for almost all stimuli, consistent with the prediction of the network model (Figure 5D, Figure 5—figure supplement 3).
evidence: This claim is based on analysis of initial and peak states presented in the study and illustrated in Figure 5D.

claim: The single-cell model predicts stronger correlations between initial and peak states, in clear conflict with the data.
source: The single-cell model instead predicts stronger correlations between initial and peak states, in clear conflict with the data (Figure 5E).
evidence: This claim is based on model predictions and comparison with data presented in the study and illustrated in Figure 5E.

claim: Pairs of stimuli with strong subspace overlaps corresponded to high connectivity overlaps, and pairs of stimuli with low subspace overlaps corresponded to low connectivity overlaps.
source: We found a close match between the two quantities (Figure 7A,B): pairs of stimuli with strong subspace overlaps corresponded to high connectivity overlaps, and pairs of stimuli with low subspace overlaps corresponded to low connectivity overlaps.
evidence: This claim is based on analysis of connectivity overlaps and subspace overlaps presented in the study and illustrated in Figure 7A and 7B.

claim: The amplification of variance is due to noise-correlations across neurons that have been previously reported in the AC.
source: This second feature demonstrates that the amplification of variance is due to noise-correlations across neurons that have been previously reported in the AC (Rothschild et al., 2010).
evidence: This claim is based on inference from analysis of trial-to-trial variability presented in the study and is consistent with previous reports.

claim: The network model reproduces both features of trial-to-trial variability observed in the data.
source: Simulations of the fitted models and a mathematical analysis show that the network model reproduces both features of trial-to-trial variability observed in the data (Figure 8E,F), based on a minimal assumption that variability originates from independent noise in the initial condition at stimulus offset (see Materials and methods, Section 'Structure of single-trial responses in the network model').
evidence: This claim is based on model simulations and analysis presented in the study and illustrated in Figure 8E and 8F.

claim: The single-cell model reproduces the first feature, the amplification of fluctuations along the same direction of state-spate as trial-averaged dynamics, although in that model the different neurons are not coupled and noise-correlations are absent.
source: Surprisingly, the single-cell model also reproduces the first feature, the amplification of fluctuations along the same direction of state-spate as trial-averaged dynamics, although in that model the different neurons are not coupled and noise-correlations are absent (Figure 8G,H).
evidence: This claim is based on model simulations and analysis presented in the study and illustrated in Figure 8G and 8H.

claim: The single-cell model fails to capture the second feature, as it produces amplified variability in both simultaneous and shuffled activity.
source: Instead, the single-cell model fails to capture the second feature, as it produces amplified variability in both simultaneous and shuffled activity.
evidence: This claim is based on model simulations and analysis presented in the study.

claim: The disagreement between the single-cell model and the data is not directly due to the lack of noise-correlations in that model, but due to the fact that the single-cell model does not predict accurately the variance of single-neuron activity during the OFF-responses.
source: Somewhat counter-intuitively, the disagreement between the single-cell model and the data is not directly due to the lack of noise-correlations in that model, but due to the fact that the single-cell model does not predict accurately the variance of single-neuron activity during the OFF-responses, and therefore fails to capture variance in shuffled activity.
evidence: This claim is based on inference from model simulations and analysis presented in the study.

claim: The network model accounts better than the single-cell model for the structure of single-trial fluctuations present in the AC data.
source: In summary, the network model accounts better than the single-cell model for the structure of single-trial fluctuations present in the AC data.
evidence: This claim is based on comparison of model predictions with data presented in the study.

claim: Strong OFF responses observed in auditory cortical neurons form transiently amplified trajectories that encode individual stimuli within low-dimensional subspaces.
source: Adopting a population approach, we showed that strong OFF responses observed in auditory cortical neurons form transiently amplified trajectories that encode individual stimuli within low-dimensional subspaces.
evidence: This is a summary of the main findings of the study based on data analysis.

claim: A geometrical analysis revealed a clear structure in the relative orientation of these subspaces, where subspaces corresponding to different auditory stimuli were largely orthogonal to each other.
source: A geometrical analysis revealed a clear structure in the relative orientation of these subspaces, where subspaces corresponding to different auditory stimuli were largely orthogonal to each other.
evidence: This is a summary of the main findings of the study based on data analysis.

claim: A simple, linear single-neuron model captures well the average response to individual stimuli, but not the structure across stimuli and across individual trials.
source: We found that a simple, linear single-neuron model captures well the average response to individual stimuli, but not the structure across stimuli and across individual trials.
evidence: This is a summary of the main findings of the study based on model fitting and comparison.

claim: A simple, linear recurrent network model accounts for all the properties of the population OFF responses, notably their global structure across multiple stimuli and the fluctuations across single trials.
source: In contrast, we showed that a simple, linear recurrent network model accounts for all the properties of the population OFF responses, notably their global structure across multiple stimuli and the fluctuations across single trials.
evidence: This is a summary of the main findings of the study based on model fitting and comparison.

claim: The results argue for a potential role of network interactions in shaping OFF responses in AC.
source: Our results therefore argue for a potential role of network interactions in shaping OFF responses in AC.
evidence: This is a conclusion drawn from the study's findings.

claim: Strong transients during stimulus onset display similar transient coding properties and could be generated by the same network mechanism as proposed for the OFF responses.
source: In this study, we focused specifically on the responses following stimulus offset. Strong transients during stimulus onset display similar transient coding properties (Mazor and Laurent, 2005) and could be generated by the same network mechanism as we propose for the OFF responses.
evidence: This is a speculation based on the study's findings and previous work.

claim: During ON-transients, a number of additional mechanisms are likely to play a role, in particular single-cell adaptation, synaptic depression, or feed-forward inhibition.
source: However, during ON-transients, a number of additional mechanisms are likely to play a role, in particular single-cell adaptation, synaptic depression, or feed-forward inhibition.
evidence: This is a statement based on established knowledge about neural mechanisms.

claim: Recent work has shown that ON and OFF trajectories elicited by a stimulus are orthogonal to each other in the state-space.
source: Indeed, recent work has shown that ON and OFF trajectories elicited by a stimulus are orthogonal to each other in the state-space (Saha et al., 2017), and this was also the case in our data set (Figure 2—figure supplement 3).
evidence: This claim is supported by citation to previous work and data from the current study.

claim: Linear network models produce ON and OFF responses that are necessarily correlated and cannot account for the observed orthogonality of ON and OFF responses for a given stimulus.
source: Linear network models instead produce ON and OFF responses that are necessarily correlated and cannot account for the observed orthogonality of ON and OFF responses for a given stimulus.
evidence: This is a statement about the limitations of linear network models based on theoretical analysis.

claim: Distinct ON and OFF response dynamics could result from intrinsic nonlinearities known to play a role in the AC.
source: Distinct ON and OFF response dynamics could also result from intrinsic nonlinearities known to play a role in the AC (Calhoun and Schreiner, 1998; Rotman et al., 2001; Sahani and Linden, 2003; Machens et al., 2004; Williamson et al., 2016; Deneux et al., 2016).
evidence: This is a speculation supported by citations to previous studies.

claim: A major assumption of both the single-cell and network models is that the AC does not receive external inputs after the auditory stimulus is removed.
source: A major assumption of both the single-cell and network models we considered is that the AC does not receive external inputs after the auditory stimulus is removed.
evidence: This is a statement about the assumptions of the models used in the study.

claim: The observation that the structure of the dynamics across stimuli could be predicted by the structure of their initial states indicates that autonomous dynamics at least partly shape the OFF responses.
source: Indeed, the observation that the structure of the dynamics across stimuli could be predicted by the structure of their initial states (Figure 2D,E and Figure 2—figure supplement 4) indicates that autonomous dynamics at least partly shape the OFF responses.
evidence: This claim is based on inference from data analysis presented in the study.

claim: Autonomous dynamics are in principle sufficient to reproduce a number of features of OFF responses in the absence of any external drive.
source: The comparisons between data and models moreover show that autonomous dynamics are in principle sufficient to reproduce a number of features of OFF responses in the absence of any external drive.
evidence: This claim is based on inference from model fitting and comparison presented in the study.

claim: Neurons in the AC do receive direct afferents from the medial geniculate body of the thalamus, and indirect input from upstream regions of the auditory pathway, where strong OFF responses have been observed.
source: However, neurons in the AC do receive direct afferents from the medial geniculate body of the thalamus, and indirect input from upstream regions of the auditory pathway, where strong OFF responses have been observed.
evidence: This is a statement based on established knowledge about auditory cortex anatomy and physiology.

claim: OFF responses observed in AC could be at least partly inherited from upstream auditory regions.
source: Thus, in principle, OFF responses observed in AC could be at least partly inherited from upstream auditory regions (Kopp-Scheinpflug et al., 2018).
evidence: This is a speculation supported by citation to previous work.

claim: A direct prediction of the network model is that the inactivation of recurrent excitation in auditory cortical areas should weaken OFF responses.
source: A direct prediction of our model is that the inactivation of recurrent excitation in auditory cortical areas should weaken OFF responses (Li et al., 2013).
evidence: This is a prediction derived from the network model and supported by citation to previous work.

claim: Recurrency in the auditory system is not present only within the cortex but also between different areas along the pathway.
source: However, recurrency in the auditory system is not present only within the cortex but also between different areas along the pathway (Ito and Malmierca, 2018; Winer et al., 1998; Lee et al., 2011).
evidence: This claim is supported by citations to previous studies.

claim: OFF responses could be generated at a higher level of recurrency and might not be abolished by inactivation of AC.
source: Therefore OFF responses could be generated at a higher level of recurrency and might not be abolished by inactivation of AC.
